concepts.name: Definition and Legal Threshold of Dumping
key_dimensions: WTO/GATT Article VI definition: export price < normal value in domestic market
De minimis threshold: dumping margin < 2% and import volume < 3% are non-actionable
Distinction between 'predatory dumping' vs 'sporadic/persistent dumping' — UPSC trap on terminology
Dumping vs subsidized exports: conceptual overlap and different remedies (anti-dumping vs countervailing duties)

concepts.name: Normal Value Determination: Methods and Hierarchy
key_dimensions: Three methods: domestic price, third-country export price, constructed value — applied in strict hierarchy
When domestic sales are insufficient (<5% rule) or distorted, constructed value is used
Non-Market Economy (NME) treatment: surrogate country methodology — India's use against China
UPSC trap: 'constructed value' includes cost of production + SGA expenses + profit, not just cost of production

concepts.name: Injury Determination in Anti-Dumping Investigations
key_dimensions: Three types of injury: material injury, threat of material injury, material retardation of domestic industry
Causation requirement: dumping must be THE cause, not just A cause — the 'non-attribution' analysis
Injury indicators: price undercutting, price suppression, market share loss, decline in profits/employment
Cumulation principle: injuries from multiple countries can be aggregated under specific conditions

concepts.name: Anti-Dumping Agreement (ADA) under WTO: Key Provisions
key_dimensions: WTO Anti-Dumping Agreement (Agreement on Implementation of Article VI of GATT 1994)
Sunset clause: duties must expire after 5 years unless sunset review justifies continuation
Mandatory lesser duty rule under EU practice vs India's discretion — UPSC comparison trap
Dispute Settlement Body (DSB) rulings on ADA — appellate body interpretations

concepts.name: India's Institutional Framework: DGTR and its Role
key_dimensions: Directorate General of Trade Remedies (DGTR) — formed in 2018 by merging DGAD, DGSG, DGSAFEGUARDS
DGTR investigates, recommends; Ministry of Finance (Department of Revenue) imposes duties — separation of powers
UPSC trap: DGTR recommends but CANNOT impose duties; Finance Ministry can reject recommendations
Timeline: initiation within 45 days of application, preliminary findings within 60 days, final within 12 months (extendable to 18)

concepts.name: Anti-Dumping Duty vs Countervailing Duty vs Safeguard Duty
key_dimensions: Anti-dumping: targets unfair pricing by foreign company; Countervailing: targets foreign government subsidies; Safeguard: targets sudden surge (no unfair trade required)
Safeguard duties apply to ALL countries (MFN basis); Anti-dumping/CVD are country/product specific — critical UPSC distinction
Can all three be applied simultaneously? — legal constraints and practical implications
WTO agreements governing each: ADA, SCM Agreement, Safeguards Agreement

concepts.name: Provisional vs Definitive Anti-Dumping Measures
key_dimensions: Provisional duties: imposed after preliminary determination, maximum 4 months (extendable to 9 months)
Definitive duties: imposed after final determination, valid for 5 years subject to sunset review
Retroactive application: can duties be applied to past imports? — limited WTO conditions
Price undertakings as alternative to duties: exporter voluntarily raises price — UPSC often tests this exception

concepts.name: Sunset Review and Mid-Term Review of Anti-Dumping Duties
key_dimensions: Sunset review: mandatory before expiry of 5 years; duty continues only if dumping/injury likely to recur
Mid-term/interim review: can be initiated anytime after 1 year if circumstances changed
New shipper review: for exporters who did not export during original investigation period
UPSC trap: sunset review does NOT automatically extend duties — it must affirmatively find likelihood of recurrence

concepts.name: Circumvention of Anti-Dumping Duties and Counter-measures
key_dimensions: Common circumvention methods: minor assembly operations in third countries, slight product modification, transshipment
Anti-circumvention investigations: India's legal framework under Customs Tariff Act
WTO gap: ADA does not explicitly address circumvention — national laws fill the vacuum
China-linked circumvention cases involving ASEAN as conduit — contemporary relevance for Prelims

concepts.name: Domestic Industry Definition and Standing to File Petition
key_dimensions: Domestic industry = producers accounting for 'major proportion' of total domestic production (not necessarily majority)
Standing threshold: petitioners must represent >25% of domestic production AND >50% of those expressing opinion
Exclusion of related importers from 'domestic industry' definition — UPSC trap
Regional industry concept: when dumped goods affect a concentrated regional market

concepts.name: India's Use of Anti-Dumping Measures: Trends and Targets
key_dimensions: India is among the top initiators of anti-dumping cases globally; China is the most frequent target
Sectors most protected: chemicals, petrochemicals, steel, textiles, pharmaceuticals
India-China trade: anti-dumping as strategic trade tool vs dependency on Chinese imports dilemma
Criticism: domestic industry protection vs consumer/downstream industry cost burden

concepts.name: Lesser Duty Rule and Public Interest Test
key_dimensions: Lesser duty rule: impose duty lower than dumping margin IF sufficient to remove injury — EU mandatory, India discretionary
India does NOT follow mandatory lesser duty rule — UPSC frequently tests this
Public interest test: some jurisdictions consider impact on consumers/downstream industries before imposing duty
India's Customs Tariff Act (CTA) 1975 and Customs Tariff (Identification, Assessment and Collection of Anti-Dumping Duty) Rules 1995

concepts.name: Special and Differential Treatment for Developing Countries under ADA
key_dimensions: Article 15 ADA: developed countries must give 'special regard' to developing country exporters — constructive remedies before duties
De minimis import volume threshold for developing countries: 4% (vs 3% for developed) before cumulation allowed
Developing country as both complainant and respondent — asymmetric application of S&D provisions
UPSC trap: S&D provisions in ADA are hortatory ('shall explore'), not binding obligations

concepts.name: Anti-Dumping in the Context of India's FTAs and Trade Agreements
key_dimensions: FTAs do NOT eliminate the right to impose anti-dumping duties — WTO rules preserved within FTA frameworks
India-ASEAN FTA: concerns about Chinese goods routed through ASEAN to circumvent anti-dumping duties
Rules of Origin requirements in FTAs as the first line of defense against circumvention
Tension between trade liberalization objectives of FTAs and protectionist use of anti-dumping

concepts.name: Judicial Review of Anti-Dumping Determinations in India
key_dimensions: CESTAT (Customs, Excise and Service Tax Appellate Tribunal) hears appeals on anti-dumping duty orders
High Courts and Supreme Court: jurisdiction on questions of law, not factual re-appreciation
Key cases: Saurashtra Chemicals vs Union of India; judicial deference to DGTR technical findings
WTO Dispute Settlement: India has been both complainant (DS436 against US) and respondent in anti-dumping disputes

concepts.name: Social and Economic Impact of Anti-Dumping Duties: Dual Effects
key_dimensions: Positive: protection of domestic jobs, infant industry support, prevention of predatory monopolization
Negative: higher input costs for downstream industries (e.g., steel duties hurting auto/construction sectors)
Consumer welfare loss vs producer surplus gain — net welfare impact often negative for importing country
UPSC policy angle: anti-dumping as 'beggar-thy-neighbor' policy and its WTO-compatibility boundaries

concepts.name: Non-Market Economy (NME) Status and Surrogate Country Methodology
key_dimensions: NME designation: government controls prices/costs, so domestic prices are unreliable for normal value calculation
Surrogate country method: use production costs from a comparable market economy country (e.g., India used for China cases by US/EU)
China's WTO accession protocol (Section 15): NME treatment was to expire in 2016 — major WTO controversy
India treats China as NME — allows higher dumping margins and more aggressive anti-dumping action

concepts.name: Anti-Dumping vs Competition Law: Interface and Overlap
key_dimensions: Predatory pricing under Competition Act 2002 vs dumping under Customs Tariff Act — different legal thresholds and remedies
Anti-dumping does not require proof of predatory intent; competition law does — UPSC trap
CCI vs DGTR jurisdiction: CCI handles domestic predatory pricing, DGTR handles import dumping
Calls for integrating trade remedy and competition policy — Doha Round unresolved issue

concepts.name: Zeroing Methodology in Dumping Margin Calculation
key_dimensions: Zeroing: treating negative dumping margins (where export price > normal value) as zero, inflating overall dumping margin
WTO Appellate Body has consistently ruled zeroing WTO-inconsistent — landmark US-Zeroing cases
Despite rulings, US continued zeroing practice — demonstrating limits of WTO enforcement
India's position on zeroing: does not formally use zeroing but calculation methodology nuances remain contested

concepts.name: Price Undertaking as Alternative to Anti-Dumping Duties
key_dimensions: Exporter voluntarily agrees to raise export price to eliminate dumping — investigation suspended/terminated
DGTR can accept price undertakings only after preliminary affirmative determination of dumping AND injury
Monitoring and enforcement challenge: breach of undertaking revives investigation and provisional duties apply retroactively
UPSC trap: price undertaking is offered by exporter, NOT imposed by importing country — it is voluntary
